title: Reconcile Dedicated vs Hosted failover orchestration and safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: We currently have two overlapping mechanisms for routing when dedicated capacity is unavailable: (A) Dedicated-first routing with an attempted spillover to hosted endpoints (implemented ad-hoc per team) and (B) global hosted spillover that routes to model variants based on cost/latency. This ticket reconciles those behaviors into a single orchestrated policy surface with clear safeguards for correctness, security, and SLO preservation.

Goals:
- Define deterministic precedence between Dedicated and Hosted for all customer tiers and regions.
- Implement pluggable safeguards that prevent silent quality regressions when spilling over across model families or quantization variants.
- Add policy knobs for region affinity, tier overrides, and per-customer opt-outs for spillover.
- Ensure observability and audit trails for every spill and fallback decision.

Scope (in-scope):
- Routing decision API changes (policy config + evaluation pipeline).
- Enforcement of token and latency budgets per request at the routing layer.
- Integration with rollback/circuit-breaker system for automated reversion if QA metrics degrade.
- Console controls (read/write) to set region preference and dedicated-first behavior per account.

Out of scope:
- Reworking lower-level serving kernels or quantizers (separate initiative).
- New dedicated capacity autoscaler (existing autoscaler will remain).
acceptance_criteria:
- Single routing decision flow used by dedicated and hosted control planes.
- No silent model family changes: any cross-family fallback logs a regression flag and emits an alert at P90 if quality metric drops >3% on customer's eval set.
- Per-account setting available in Console: dedicated_preference = [dedicated_first|hosted_first|region_strict].
- Circuit-breaker trips when per-route quality or latency SLOs are violated for 5m sustained.
- End-to-end e2e test that simulates a dedicated pool outage and validates correct spillover with audit entries in logs.
- Feature flags present to rollback routing changes without infra deploy.
tasks: Design policy schema: priority, region_affinity, model_variant_constraints, quality_thresholds
Implement routing decision engine extension and API (server + protobuf contract)
Add token + latency budget enforcement at ingress
Hook into eval pipeline to run lightweight quality checks on spilled responses
Console UI: per-account routing preference toggle and audit viewer
End-to-end integration tests and chaos test (simulate dedicated pool outage)
Security review and threat model update
Docs: PRD + README for runtime configuration
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off triage. Collected customer reports where hosted spillover returned quantized variants that failed strict JSON schema validations. Need a schema-level guard.

2026-02-25 - Luis Romero: Spike complete. Verified current hosted spillover allows cross-family fallbacks without a per-request quality check. PR for policy schema sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ENG/ENG-9137-schema-draft
2026-03-02 - Mary Chen (PM): Reviewed initial design. Requested explicit per-customer opt-out label and enforcement of region_strict for regulated accounts. Added parent PM-442.
2026-03-07 - Security (Jonah Blake): Raised concern about auditability for on-prem Private deployments; routing decisions must include an opaque decision-id included in audit logs for traceability.
2026-03-11 - Luis Romero: Implemented budget enforcement prototype. Pushed branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2234
2026-03-13 - QA (Tina Vu): Ran chaos test. Observed that circuit-breaker tripping did not propagate to Console toggle; filed follow-up ENG-9150 to wire UI state.

decision_log: 2026-02-27: Decided 'dedicated_first' is default for Enterprise & Platform accounts; 'hosted_first' allowed for self-serve developer tier.
2026-03-03: Agreed on model_variant_constraints: fallbacks must be within the same model family or have validated schema compatibility unless explicit opt-in.
2026-03-08: Chose to run lightweight eval (synthetic prompt set) at routing time only for cross-family fallbacks to avoid per-request latency blowup.
2026-03-10: Circuit-breaker policy: trip on sustained SLO violations (5 minute window) and annotate decision-id in audit logs for rollback tracing.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): 5% of enterprise accounts in us-west, dedicated_first policy enforced; monitor spillover rate and quality deltas for 48h. Phase 2: Expand to all enterprise in US regions, enable per-account override in Console. Phase 3: Default apply to self-serve tier; enable hosted_first opt-in. Rollback via feature flag 'routing.v2.enabled' and immediate manual circuit-breaker toggle.
qa_notes: QA harness includes: synthetic eval set (customer-like prompts), chaos script to kill dedicated pools, and a regression test to ensure no schema-mismatched responses on JSON-structured endpoints. Test keys: route-death-test-2026. Expectation: alarm fired when quality delta >3% and circuit-breaker triggers within 5m.
implementation_risks:
- Cross-family fallbacks can produce semantic drift; mitigated by lightweight evals and conservative default policies.
- Extra routing latency for eval checks if not batched; mitigated by caching previous check results per model-variant pair.
- Console rollout complexity for private deployments: we will surface read-only view and require signed config pushes for on-prem.
next_steps:

notes_for_release: Include migration guide for customers who have custom spillover hooks. Announce per-account toggles and the 'region_strict' option with clear docs on behavior and SLO consequences.
